chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The People of the Book and all those who have a covenant (dhimmah), if one of the two spouses becomes a Muslim, they remain upon their marriage, and it is not for him to expel her from the House of Islam to another, nor should he spend the night with her, but he should come to her during the day.

As for the Polytheists, such as the polytheists of the Arabs and others, they remain upon their marriage until the expiry of the waiting period (iddah). If the woman becomes a Muslim, then the man becomes a Muslim before the expiry of her term, she is his wife; but if he does not become a Muslim except after the expiry of the term, she has been irrevocably divorced from him, and there is no way for him to her.

And similarly is all those who have no covenant, nor is it befitting for the Muslim man to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman when he can find a Muslim woman, whether she is free or a slave girl.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.العِدَّةِ: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.ذِمَّةٌ: Covenant/Protection (status of non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)
key_terms.يَبِيتَ مَعَهَا: To spend the night with her (consummation/cohabitation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a Muslim man to a Jewish or Christian woman if he can find a Muslim woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of *Istibra'* (waiting period) in mixed-faith marriages, distinguishing between *Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book) and *Mushrikun* (Polytheists). It establishes that for People of the Book, the marriage bond persists but cohabitation is suspended during the waiting period, whereas for Polytheists, the marriage dissolves automatically upon the expiry of the period if the other spouse has not converted. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view on the validity of existing marital contracts upon conversion and the practical implications for daily interaction between spouses.
